newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH UNIONS WANT MORE NUCLEAR AND HYDRO POWER.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH UNIONS WANT MORE NUCLEAR AND HYDRO POWER.

text.p: A group of Finnish industrial unions on Friday repeated their call for political decisions to allow the building of more nuclear and hydro power capacity.
Finland should not commit itself to further reduce emissions of carbon dioxide before 2010 because any such move would hurt domestic growth and employment, the union group said in a statement.
"Our country needs a real shift in energy policy. "Parliament should grant this year permits to expand nuclear and hydro power," it added.
Even a modest target of on average two percent annual growth to 2010 would require an increase in electricity production of 300 megawatt per year, the unions said.
More nuclear power could come on stream at the earliest after 2005, while any significant increase in natural gas power production could be feasible at the earliest five years later.
"For once we should be honest ... and recognise the fact that Finland cannot reduce its own carbon dioxide emissions by 2010 without damages to economic growth and employment," the unions said.
